samples.summary: New command-level test isolates WAFFLEBASE_CONFIG but not WAFFLEBASE_SESSION, so the test process can read (and, on one reachable path, overwrite) the real ~/.wafflebase/session.json credential file
samples.evidence: The new `describe('--quiet does not suppress the body or the error envelope')` block overrides only `WAFFLEBASE_CONFIG`, `WAFFLEBASE_API_KEY`, `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER`, `WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE` (test/output.test.ts:181-201) and comments that this makes the resolved config come "purely from these env vars — no developer's ~/.wafflebase leaks in". That claim is not true of the session file: `getSessionPath()` (packages/cli/src/config/session.ts:38-41) falls back to `join(homedir(), '.wafflebase', 'session.json')` and is *not* affected by `WAFFLEBASE_CONFIG`; only `WAFFLEBASE_SESSION` isolates it. Today the real session file happens not to be read because `resolveConfig` short-circuits on the API-key env var at packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:86-103 before reaching `loadSession()` at config.ts:111. The isolation is therefore accidental, and the comment records the opposite. Concretely, if any future case in this block drops `WAFFLEBASE_API_KEY` (or resolution order changes), `resolveConfig` takes the JWT branch, loads the developer's/CI runner's live access+refresh tokens into the test process, and — because `stubFetch` returns `ok: true` with an arbitrary JSON body — a 401 would drive `HttpClient.refreshSession` (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:85-91) to `saveSession()` mock tokens over the real credential file. The sibling suite already does the right thing: packages/cli/test/config.test.ts:15-16 and :25-26 override both `WAFFLEBASE_CONFIG` and `WAFFLEBASE_SESSION`.
searchedFor: Grep 'WAFFLEBASE_SESSION|WAFFLEBASE_CONFIG' across packages/cli (only config.test.ts sets WAFFLEBASE_SESSION; the new test does not)
Read packages/cli/vitest-adjacent tests: config.test.ts env isolation pattern

samples.summary: `api-keys create --quiet` now unconditionally writes freshly minted plaintext API key material to stdout; the PR's new tests lock the "quiet never suppresses the body" rule in without carving out the one command whose body is a live credential
samples.evidence: The PR removes the `quiet` gate from `output()` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:26-28) and the new tests in test/output.test.ts:246-281 pin that behavior at the command level. `api-keys create` prints the server response verbatim via `output(res.data, opts.format)` (packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:19), and the backend's create endpoint (packages/backend/src/api-key/api-key.controller.ts:25-41 -> ApiKeyService.create) is the only place the plaintext key is ever returned. Before this change, `wafflebase api-keys create x --quiet` kept the secret off stdout; after it, the secret lands on stdout in every quiet/scripted context (CI logs, `set -x` transcripts, tee'd output). This is arguably the intended contract (the body is the data the caller redirects), so it is a hardening note, not a defect — but if the body is meant to be unsuppressible, the secret-bearing command deserves an explicit decision rather than inheriting the rule silently.

samples.summary: User-supplied doc-id / tab-id / cell ref are interpolated raw into request paths (no encodeURIComponent), letting `..`, `?` and `#` retarget the request outside the workspace base path
samples.evidence: `getCell`/`setCell`/`deleteCell`/`getCells`/`getDocument` build `/documents/${docId}/tabs/${tabId}/cells/${sref}` with no encoding (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:218-233, 153-161), and the values come straight from argv (packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:16-24, packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:113-118). `wafflebase docs get '../../../../workspaces/OTHER/api-keys'` sends the caller's Authorization header to a path outside `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${workspace}`. No privilege boundary is crossed (the caller already owns the credential and the server still authorizes), so this is hardening only. Pre-existing and untouched by this delta; the delta's new tests (`sheets cells get doc-1 A1`, `docs get doc-1`) are the first coverage to drive these path builders end-to-end, which is why I am noting it here.
